proposer.mechanism: PROTECTIVE-STOP attachment layered on position-tier-gate (cap=1 verbatim). When an OPEN order passes the cap=1 gate, BEFORE submitting it, capture the arrival-mid price from cache.quote_tick(instrument_id) and compute stop_price = arrival_mid - stop_ticks*tick_size for BUY (or + for SELL), with stop_ticks=2 (i.e. 2*0.25 = 0.50 points = $2.50 loss cap on MES). Submit the OPEN as before, then submit a contingent reduce-only StopMarketOrder at stop_price for the same quantity. When the oracle's natural CLOSE arrives at t+1s, it either (a) finds the stop has already fired and the position is flat (CLOSE becomes a no-op / rejected reduce-only), or (b) the stop has not fired and the CLOSE executes normally, in which case we also need to cancel the working stop order. Track stop_order_id per position; in on_position_closed() (or on_order_filled for the close leg), cancel any open stop for that position. This caps each individual losing trade's magnitude while leaving winning trades unchanged. CLOSE orders themselves always submit unchanged.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Loss-magnitude asymmetry. The base wins 37.2% of round trips. For the base to net $4262.50 with 90,433 round trips (mean $0.047/trade), winners must average roughly $0.40 and losers average roughly $-0.20 (algebraically, with W=fraction wins=0.372: 0.372*$Wmag + 0.628*(-$Lmag) = $0.047, so $Wmag/$Lmag ratio of ~2 is consistent with $Wmag≈$0.18, $Lmag≈$0.09 in the simplest case, but the per-day range $168 to $551 implies more spread). The 1-second oracle holding window means each loser drifts adversely by some random amount before the next CLOSE - capping that drift via a stop converts the tail of the loss distribution into a fixed-magnitude loss. Even if 10% of losers historically drift beyond 2 ticks within 1 second, capping their loss at 2 ticks ($2.50) vs an uncapped 4-5 tick adverse drift ($5-6.25) lifts per-trade PnL by ~$0.20-0.40 * 0.10 * 0.628 ≈ $0.015-0.025/trade ≈ +30-50% on the base's $0.047/trade.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Mean slippage stays 0 and commissions stay 0 in this simulator (verified from base backtest-results.json: total_commissions=0.0, mean_slippage=0.0). StopMarketOrder fills at trigger_price exactly under deterministic replay with slippage=0. Adding a stop order does not introduce execution costs. The mechanism strictly reduces loss magnitudes (stops fire only on adverse drift) and leaves winners untouched (their natural CLOSE executes before any adverse drift hits the stop, by definition of being a winner).
proposer.builds_on: position-tier-gate (cap=1 retained verbatim as the gate for OPENs; stop attachment is an additive execution behavior triggered AFTER the gate allows the OPEN). Materially different from both prior PC runs which were SELECTION filters (skip trades): this is a LOSS-CAPPING mechanism (every signal still executes; only losers are size-capped). Different axis entirely.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) r1 signal-consensus filter and r2 loss-cooldown: both were SELECTION filters along the trade-count axis; r1 was empirically inert, r2 lost -6.1% PnL. Filtering apparently drops winners as often as losers when applied symmetrically. Declined. (2) Adaptive stop distance (volatility-scaled, e.g. ATR(N)): adds parameters; reserve for follow-up if fixed stop works. (3) Trailing stop (move stop up as position becomes profitable): asymmetric mechanism that also caps winner profits; declined - we want to leave winners alone. (4) Scale-out at +N ticks profit: caps WINNERS not losers; opposite of what we want given 37% win rate. (5) Time-decay stop (tighten as holding period approaches t+1s): the oracle's natural CLOSE arrives at t+1s anyway; redundant. (6) Take-profit alongside stop: bidirectional bracket would cap winners and losers symmetrically - net zero or negative since the win/loss asymmetry is what makes the strategy profitable. Declined. (7) Looser stop (5 ticks): less likely to fire, smaller impact; reserved for tuning. (8) Tighter stop (1 tick): too noisy, would fire on normal microstructure jitter even on winning trades. Declined.

objections.text: Nautilus ExecAlgorithm API incompatibility for contingent stops. Verified via inspect: ExecAlgorithm exposes only spawn_market, spawn_limit, spawn_market_to_limit (and submit_order/cancel_order/modify_order). There is NO spawn_stop or order_factory attribute on the exec algo. To submit a StopMarketOrder, the algorithm must manually construct one with trader_id, strategy_id, ClientOrderId, UUID4, ts_init, trigger_price, trigger_type, exec_algorithm_id, etc. - derivable from self.trader_id, the parent order, self.clock, but a substantial implementation burden the Proposer did not specify. A cleaner path the Proposer ignored: subscribe_quote_ticks() in on_start() and monitor every quote in on_quote_tick(); when adverse drift exceeds the threshold, submit a reduce-only MarketOrder via spawn_market(primary=self._open_order_for_position, ...) or a manually constructed MarketOrder. Either way, the proposal's terse 'submit a contingent reduce-only StopMarketOrder' is under-specified for the actual API surface.

Loss-magnitude asymmetry claim is unverified and the math is hand-wavy. Per the base backtest-results.json, realized_pnl=$4262.50 over 90,433 trades = $0.047/trade. Win rate=37.2%. With Wmag=avg-win, Lmag=avg-loss: 0.372*Wmag - 0.628*Lmag = $0.047. This has infinitely many solutions. Without measuring the empirical loss distribution (analysis skill exists; Proposer did not use it), we don't know if (a) most losers are already < 2 ticks (in which case the 2-tick stop is a no-op and the mechanism is INERT, repeating the r1 trap), (b) most losers exceed 2 ticks (in which case the stop helps), or (c) the loss distribution has heavy tails that even the 2-tick stop barely touches. The Proposer's quoted 30-50% PnL improvement is constructed without evidence. Mitigation: failure mode is bounded (worst case is no improvement, since stops only fire on adverse drift), so an empirical test is informative. Acceptable risk only because the downside is bounded.

Premature-stop hazard: oracle's natural 1-second hold likely sees adverse intratrade drift on MANY winners that ultimately mean-revert by t+1s close. With the oracle's R^2 ~14% (sigma=6.0), even a 'correct' signal has substantial noise on the path. A 2-tick stop (= 0.50 points on MES; ESM6 1-second realized vol is plausibly 0.1-0.5 points) is comparable to one-second normal drift. The mechanism could convert eventually-winning trades into realized losses on their adverse-drift path. The Proposer did not measure 1-second adverse-drift quantiles or the empirical noise floor. Suggest a wider stop (5-10 ticks) so the stop only fires on genuine tail moves, not normal one-second jitter. Without this calibration, the mechanism could DEGRADE PnL by destroying winners' natural mean-reversion.

Stop-cancellation race / order-list lifecycle not specified. When the oracle's CLOSE arrives at t+1s, the stop is still working at the venue. Three failure modes the Proposer did not address: (a) The CLOSE reduces position to 0 first, then the stop becomes orphaned (reduce-only on flat position - rejected? or sits as a working order that could trigger later, breaching intraday_flat?). (b) The stop fires at t+0.7s, the position is flat, and the oracle's CLOSE at t+1s also tries to reduce zero - rejected? Or partially fills the next OPEN? (c) Mapping from position -> stop_order_id: with concurrent oracle ticks, multiple opens/stops in flight, the algorithm needs explicit tracking. The Proposer waves this away with 'in on_position_closed cancel any open stop' but the API for tracking and cancelling needs concrete spec. If the stop is not reliably cancelled, surviving orphan stops could fire on the NEXT position's adverse drift, causing a double-exit and a phantom inverse position.

Superior alternative not considered: ASYMMETRIC HOLD-PERIOD EXTENSION on PROFITABLE positions. Instead of capping losers, EXTEND winners. When on_quote_tick() shows the position is in the green by >= N_take_ticks at t < 1s, suppress the next oracle CLOSE for this position (or convert it to a no-op) and continue holding until either (a) the position drops back to break-even, or (b) a TRAILING stop at +N/2 ticks fires. This exploits the same asymmetric-magnitude argument the Proposer cites but on the WIN side - where the oracle's R^2 is the real signal source, profitable positions are more likely to continue than reverse. Failure mode is symmetric to the stop proposal (worst case is no improvement), but the upside is theoretically larger because winners are 37% of trades and there's no premature-stop hazard. The Proposer did not consider this. Note: this is technically harder to implement (needs to suppress the oracle's CLOSE, which exec algo can't trivially do - but can be approximated by not yet closing and letting the next oracle OPEN net-trade through). The simpler version: just add a take-profit AND stop pair (bracket) but the Proposer explicitly declined brackets without measuring.

arrival_mid sourcing: the Proposer says 'capture arrival-mid price from cache.quote_tick(instrument_id)'. This works only if subscribe_quote_ticks() was called in on_start(). Otherwise cache.quote_tick() returns the last quote the engine fed to the algorithm (which might or might not be the most recent). Acceptable scaffolding concern.

suggested_alternatives: Quote-tick-monitored synthetic stop using spawn_market or manually-constructed reduce-only MarketOrder fired from on_quote_tick when adverse drift exceeds N ticks (avoids the StopMarketOrder construction complexity).
Wider stop (5-10 ticks) calibrated to be outside the 1-second noise floor, so only tail-drift losers are capped, not winners' natural intratrade adverse path.
Asymmetric hold-extension on profitable positions: a take-profit-trail mechanism that lets winners run beyond the oracle's natural 1-second close.

Empirical analysis of the 1-second adverse-drift distribution on a 2-3 training dates BEFORE choosing the stop threshold (use the analysis skill; it's available for exactly this kind of hypothesis-grounding question).
criticizer.reasoning: The mechanism is coherent in spirit but BLOCKING on the API spec (no spawn_stop) and the stop threshold is uncalibrated against the empirical 1-second drift distribution, risking premature stops that destroy winners. The cancellation race and stop-orphaning failure modes need concrete handling. A quote-tick-monitored synthetic stop or asymmetric hold-extension on winners would address these. Revise.

proposer.mechanism: WINNERS-RUN gate: skip the oracle's CLOSE order when the position is currently profitable and has been held less than max_extend_seconds. Concretely, on each on_order(CLOSE) with is_reduce_only=True: (1) find the matching open Position via cache.positions_open(instrument_id); (2) compute unrealized_pnl from current quote (cache.quote_tick(instrument_id).bid_price for LONG exit valuation, ask for SHORT) minus avg_px_open; (3) compute hold_duration_ns = clock.timestamp_ns() - position.ts_opened; (4) if unrealized_pnl > 0 AND hold_duration_ns < max_extend_ns (default 60s), SKIP this CLOSE - do NOT submit. Otherwise SUBMIT the CLOSE normally. The position remains open; subsequent oracle OPENs at later ticks are blocked by the existing position-tier-gate cap=1 mechanism (verbatim retained), so the algorithm holds the winner until either (a) the next oracle CLOSE arrives with the position now at break-even or red (CLOSE submits, exits), or (b) the hold duration exceeds max_extend_ns (force-exit at the first eligible CLOSE), or (c) end-of-session intraday_flat forces a close. CLOSE orders on losing or stale positions submit unchanged. OPEN orders go through the unmodified cap=1 gate.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Empirically measured (via analysis of positions.csv across all 12 train dates): position duration is strongly correlated with profitability. Positions held 1-2s yield -$0.024/trade avg (30.8% win rate), 5-10s yield +$0.058/trade (41.2% win), 30-60s yield +$0.817/trade (58.7% win), 60-600s yield +$0.922/trade (59.5% win). Position duration of 30+ seconds accounts for $2,157 of total $4,262 base PnL (51%) while being only 2.8% of trades. The mechanism: oracle short-holds are mostly the choppy flip-flop noise; oracle long-holds are sustained directional signals where the oracle is actually confident. By skipping the first CLOSE on a profitable short-hold, we attempt to convert short noisy positions into longer-hold profitable ones. Critically, we condition on CURRENT profitability (unrealized_pnl > 0 at the CLOSE moment), so we only extend trades that the path-evolution has already validated as 'going our way'. The break-even-stop dynamic (exit when goes red) caps the risk of converted winners reverting to losers - they exit at break-even when the next oracle CLOSE fires on a position no longer in the green.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Mean slippage stays 0 and commissions stay 0 in this simulator (verified from base backtest-results.json). The mechanism only changes the FILTERING of CLOSE submissions and adds no new orders - no execution-cost surface change. The only economic risk is missed reversals: when we skip a CLOSE on a profitable position, the oracle was signaling that the position should be closed (likely because oracle now thinks direction will reverse). If the oracle is right at that moment, the position drifts back into the red and exits at break-even on the next CLOSE - small loss of the original unrealized gain but no negative realized PnL. If the oracle was wrong (false flip signal in a sustained-direction regime), we capture additional drift in our favor. The asymmetry: oracle R^2 ~14% means most individual signals are noise; sustained-direction regimes are where the real edge lives, and they are exactly the regimes where 'flip' signals are most likely to be false alarms.
proposer.builds_on: position-tier-gate (cap=1 retained verbatim as the OPEN gate). Pivots from r1 (signal-consensus filter, inert) and r2 (loss-cooldown, -6.1% PnL) which both filtered OPENs symmetrically; this filters CLOSEs ASYMMETRICALLY conditional on path-evolution evidence (unrealized_pnl > 0). Different axis entirely.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Protective stop on losers (round 1 proposal): empirical analysis of positions.csv shows 99% of losers are <=2 ticks, ideal 2-tick stop saves only +4.5% (under gate), and the IDEAL is an upper bound since stops fire on intratrade adverse drift not just ultimate losers. Dropped. (2) Wider stop (5+ ticks): saves <0.1% (essentially no losers exceed 5 ticks). Dropped. (3) Synthetic stop via on_quote_tick monitoring (criticizer's suggestion): same problem - the loss distribution is too tight. (4) Time-based forced extension (always hold N seconds): blind to current-profitability evidence; would hold losers as well as winners, likely net negative. (5) Conditional on UNREALIZED_PNL >= K_ticks instead of >0: stricter threshold; risks missing the long-tail winners that start small. >0 is the cleanest trigger. (6) Conditional on hold_duration >= MIN_HOLD (extend only old positions): contradicts the goal of extending SHORT positions into long ones. (7) Take-profit at +K_ticks instead of skip-on-profitable: caps the right tail (winners >5t generate $809), opposite of what we want. (8) Hybrid (skip CLOSE if green AND hold_duration in [N_min, N_max]): adds parameter; reserved for tuning if base mechanism passes.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 1 BLOCKING (API spec for StopMarketOrder): no longer applicable - new mechanism uses only filtering of incoming CLOSE orders, no order construction. Round 1 MAJOR (asymmetric edge math hand-wavy): replaced with empirical analysis of positions.csv across all 12 train dates - duration vs PnL correlation is the dominant empirical signal, much stronger than the loss-magnitude angle. Round 1 MAJOR (premature-stop hazard): no stops in new mechanism. Round 1 MAJOR (stop-cancellation race): no contingent orders in new mechanism. Round 1 MAJOR (superior alternative - asymmetric hold extension on winners): ADOPTED directly as the new mechanism, with the elegant implementation via skipping the natural CLOSE rather than constructing new orders. Round 1 MINOR (arrival_mid sourcing via subscribe_quote_ticks in on_start): yes, will subscribe in on_start and fall back to position.avg_px_open if quote unavailable (degrades to 'never extend' rather than crashing - safe default). The new mechanism is materially different from round 1: simpler, empirically grounded, and uses Nautilus's natural order flow rather than constructing contingent orders.

objections.text: Selection-bias confound in the duration->PnL correlation. The Proposer cites that 30-60s held positions yield +$0.817/trade. BUT in the base algo, a position lasts 30-60s ONLY when the oracle keeps signaling the SAME direction for 30+ seconds without issuing a CLOSE. That is, long-duration positions are SELECTED by the oracle's sustained-direction signal. The Proposer's mechanism does the inverse: it forces hold on positions where the oracle JUST issued a CLOSE (i.e., the oracle is signaling reversal). The duration-PnL correlation in the data is conditional on oracle-confirmed direction; force-extending against an oracle reversal signal is a different population. We cannot expect those forced-hold positions to inherit the long-hold profitability. The Proposer's 'condition on unrealized_pnl > 0' partly addresses this (path evidence overrides oracle reversal), but the fundamental confound remains: empirically, the 1-2s population that the mechanism targets has avg PnL -$0.024 and 30.8% win rate. We have NO empirical evidence that the subset of these with unrealized_pnl > 0 AT CLOSE MOMENT continues to be profitable if held longer.

Missed-reversal opportunity cost. When the oracle issues CLOSE+OPEN at the same ts_init for a flipped signal, the CLOSE realizes existing PnL and the OPEN bets on the new direction. The base algo's cap=1 mechanism already SKIPS the OPEN (because position is still open), so the algorithm doesn't take the reversal bet. BUT the base does REALIZE the CLOSE's PnL. The new mechanism: skip the CLOSE on a profitable position, miss the OPEN (cap=1 blocks it anyway), and hope to extend the held position. If the oracle is right about the reversal, the held position drifts back to break-even or red, we exit with little/no gain (and missed the chance to flip-and-profit on the reversal-direction bet). If the oracle is wrong, we get a small additional gain. The expected value depends on oracle hit rate on reversal signals, which we have NO measurement of. The hypothesis is implicitly: 'oracle reversal signals are noisier than oracle stable signals' - plausible but unverified for THIS oracle (sigma=6.0). Acceptable empirical risk because failure mode is bounded (worst case is matching base PnL when extended holds revert to break-even), but the upside claim is speculative.

Quote-tick subscription and unrealized_pnl computation. The Proposer says 'subscribe quote ticks in on_start' and 'compute unrealized_pnl from cache.quote_tick().bid_price for LONG exit'. Three issues: (a) cache.quote_tick() returns the LATEST quote in cache, which may be older than the current ts_event of the CLOSE order. If quote_tick last update was 200ms ago and the market has moved, the unrealized_pnl calculation is stale. (b) bid_price for LONG exit valuation is correct for SELL-to-close, but the Proposer should verify position.side and use the appropriate side - getting this wrong inverts the green/red decision for SHORT positions. (c) Fallback behavior 'degrades to never extend' if quote unavailable: stated as 'safe default' but at session start the first few orders may have no quote in cache yet, so the mechanism is silently disabled for those - acceptable but should be logged. None are BLOCKING; tighten in implementation.

max_extend_seconds = 60 truncates the long-hold tail. Empirical data shows 60-600s held positions yield +$0.922/trade across 939 positions = $865.50 total - this is a meaningful piece of base PnL. With max_extend=60s, every position that naturally would have held longer in the base will be FORCED to exit at the first eligible CLOSE after 60s, possibly at a worse price than the natural eventual oracle CLOSE. Two issues: (a) loss of the >60s upside, (b) potential for the 60s-truncation point to be a microstructure-unfavorable moment. Suggest no upper cap (or a much wider cap like 30 minutes) with end-of-session safety: detect when clock is within X minutes of session close and force-submit any pending CLOSE. The intraday_flat constraint is enforced by the strategy itself at end-of-session, not by the exec algo, so likely the strategy issues a final CLOSE that always submits - check this assumption. If verified, max_extend can be removed entirely.

Risk of compounding the extension. If we extend a position multiple times (CLOSE arrives, skip because green; later CLOSE arrives, position still green, skip again; etc.), the position could stay open indefinitely until red. This is the intended 'break-even stop' dynamic, but it's worth verifying the chain works: the second CLOSE order arrives because the oracle re-issued a flip signal (oracle wants to reverse direction), so multiple CLOSEs on the same position = repeated oracle reversal signals against us. If the position remains profitable through multiple oracle reversals, that is by hypothesis a sustained-direction win. Logic OK; verify implementation handles repeat skips correctly.

Failure-mode boundedness. Worst case: mechanism extends a position that immediately reverts to break-even, exits with 0 gain instead of the +$0.50 it would have realized at the natural CLOSE. Loss is bounded per trade by the magnitude of unrealized_pnl at the time of the skipped CLOSE. Per the winners distribution, q50 winner = $0.50, so per-extension downside is bounded around $0.50. Acceptable risk.

suggested_alternatives: Empirical-grounded calibration: before implementation, look at the joint distribution of (unrealized_pnl at first CLOSE arrival, duration to natural close, ultimate realized PnL). The analysis skill could pull this from fills.csv joined with positions.csv to estimate the actual conditional improvement.
Remove max_extend cap (unbounded extend with end-of-session safety), to retain the 60-600s long-hold upside.

Verify quote_tick subscription updates in real time within the deterministic replay - if cache returns stale quotes, fallback to position.avg_px_open with a small adverse buffer (e.g., is_green if (unrealized_pnl > +1 tick) to provide noise margin).
criticizer.reasoning: The mechanism is empirically grounded (the duration-PnL correlation is real and well-measured), the failure mode is concretely bounded (per-trade downside ~$0.50 of foregone realized winners that revert), and the residual concerns are calibration/implementation details rather than structural flaws. The selection-bias confound is the main scientific risk, but the conditional on unrealized_pnl > 0 partly mitigates it, and the experiment is well-formed to discover whether the effect holds in the forced-extension population. No clearly superior untried alternative remains apparent for the asymmetric-hold axis. Suggest removing max_extend_seconds cap (or widening to capture the 60-600s tail) and verifying quote_tick subscription behavior at implementation time.
